key_insight: In thin 316L stainless-steel foils, laser keyhole instability can trigger hole nucleation and rapid hole growth once line energy rises beyond the stable welding regime.
engineering_relevance: The results define practical energy thresholds for avoiding perforation in thin-sheet laser welding and provide a geometric criterion for suppressing cut formation.
method: High-speed imaging of bead-on-plate laser welding on 200 μm foils representing 100 μm overlap-sheet joints
Systematic variation of line energy to link keyhole instability, hole nucleation, and hole growth
Geometric Young–Laplace force-balance analysis of hole shape and stability
evidence_signal: Continuous seams were achieved up to about 7 kJ/m, holes appeared above this range, and cutting dominated above about 12 kJ/m, with holes growing at roughly 0.8–1.2 m/s over 1–3 ms.
watch_item: The reported thresholds are specific to the tested foil thickness, geometry, and material, so direct transfer to other alloys or thicknesses needs validation.
paper_title: Rupture and growth of holes in the melt pool during laser keyhole welding of thin sheets
